findings: All four frozen source variants are covered; the variant that also asks which MySQL storage engines exist is answered with version-bound examples plus SHOW ENGINES runtime discovery rather than a timeless fixed list.

MySQL 8.4 documents InnoDB as the default transaction-safe engine with commit, rollback, crash recovery, row-level locking, consistent nonlocking reads, clustered indexes and foreign-key support; the candidate stays within those contracts.

MySQL 8.4 documents MyISAM as table-level-locking and commonly suited to read-only/read-mostly workloads, while its feature table marks transactions and MVCC unsupported; the candidate preserves those boundaries without claiming zero conditional concurrency.
The candidate correctly avoids the false simplification that InnoDB always locks exactly one row: MySQL documents record/range/next-key locking based on scanned index ranges.
Version-sensitive pitfalls are handled: the answer rejects the obsolete MyISAM-only FULLTEXT claim and avoids universal performance rankings.

Concept completeness is sufficient: default selection, transaction/recovery, concurrency/MVCC, foreign keys, index organization, runtime engine discovery, selection conditions, caveats and follow-up questions are all present.
No fabricated project metrics or personal production history are asserted.
